text:
maria: Heads up — saw a spike in GPU-pod evictions in eu-west1 this morning. Not the normal packing churn. Ops alert showed a bunch of 0/1 NIC egress saturation on nodes with free GPUs.
kai: Hmm. You mean nodes with idle GPU capacity but high egress usage from other pods? :thinking_face:
maria: Exactly. Scheduler sees GPU free and schedules large-gang pods, but runtime/drivers report egress queuing and NVLink retransmits later, then kubelet OOMKill/evict cascade for tiny pods, and bigger jobs end up Preempted. Logs: "netdev transmit queue timeout" around same window.
devin: Can you paste the alert IDs? ops-bot: alert 8912, 8913 correlated to egress.bandwidth.percent > 90 on nodes labeled zone=eu-west1-b
maria: alert 8912
maria: quick dump:
```
$ kubectl top node eu-node-42
NAME        CPU(cores)   CPU%   MEMORY(bytes)   MEMORY%   egress_mbps
eu-node-42  1200m        30%    64Gi            45%       720
```
node had 2 free GPUs but egress saturated at 720 Mbps (we usually cap 500 for mixed-tenant racks)
kai: sounds like network vs gpu co-scheduling mismatch. Scheduler only considers GPU/CPU/memory. We do have nic labels but not weighted in binpack.
devin: And NVLink/NIC contention is emergent when we pack multi-gang GPU workloads next to high-egress streaming preprocessors.
maria: Result: small service pods get evicted -> rollbacks -> more churn -> capacity appears fragmented. Cost: we had ~18% higher preempt/retry for large jobs last 6h.
kai: Short-term mitigation: taint nodes suffering high egress to prefer moving streaming pods off gpu nodes. Could run a cron to push taint when egress > 600mbps.
maria: Proposal patch snippet:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: taint-offloader
spec:
  containers:
  - name: monitor
    image: redwood/egress-taint:latest
```
(daemon can add taint: network-heavy=true:NoSchedule)

devin: Also add a scheduler predicate to avoid placing large multi-gang GPU workloads onto nodes with egress_mbps > X. We already export egress_mbps in node-metrics.
kai: We should avoid changing core scheduler abruptly. Suggest: implement a plugin as a score tweak and rollout as feature-flagged alpha.
maria: Rollout plan idea:
- Canary: enable score tweak in eu-west1 only for 1 month, 10% of nodes (label canary=true)
- Run SLO: eviction_rate < 1.5x baseline, job retry <= 5%
- Revert path: remove plugin flag and taint cron

devin: For immediate relief I can run a one-off script to cordon top-5 noisy nodes and drain non-gang pods to warmpool nodes. That should reduce the NVLink collisions.
ops-bot: runbook recommend: /runbooks/network-egress-gpu-collisions -> step 2: cordon noisy nodes, step 3: apply network QoS ingress/egress shaping
sre-runbook-bot: creating incident note in #incidents with correlation id inc-20260305-egressgpu
maria: Who can own the canary plugin PR? @kai? kai: I can start a draft today. Will open a KEP-ish doc with perf measurement hooks.
devin: I'll own the rapid cordon/relocation script and post it to runbook once tested.
maria: Thanks — let's track cost delta and evictions metric. If canary stabilizes, we roll to ap-southeast (last time we saw similar pattern there).
kai: one more: can we enrich node labels with rack-egress-capacity so scheduler knows hot racks? Could help cross-az packing.
maria: Good call. I'll add a telemetry item to infra backlog.
devin: TL;DR: network congestion + naive GPU binpacking = ghost-free GPUs but evicting workloads. Fix path: taint/cordon short-term, scheduler scoring + node egress labels medium-term. :white_check_mark:
